newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN slams Bosnian Serbs for trial of journalist.
newsitem.headline: UN slams Bosnian Serbs for trial of journalist.

text.p: A United Nations spokesman on Friday accused Bosnian Serbs of disregarding civil rights and legal standards for prosecuting a journalist.
He also hit out at Moslem authorities for their illegal detention of a Serb man.

The criticism came after a Bosnian Serb court on Thursday found a journalist guilty of libel against local authorities for publishing a story accusing the Serb ruling party of organising the disruption of opposition campaign rallies.
A second journalist was acquitted, without explanation, by the court in the central town of Doboj in Serb-held territory, said human rights workers in the Open Media Research Institute.
Both defendants worked for the independent weekly newspaper Alternativa based in Doboj in Bosnia's Serb republic.
The court sentenced Zivko Savkovic, managing editor of Alternativa, to one year probation.

"It's very unfortunate that one of the few independent newspapers published in the Serb republic is being harassed in such a manner and is being investigated," Aleksandar Ivanko, a United Nations spokesman, told Reuters.
"It shows how abysmal the situation is in (the Serb republic) regarding the media and human rights of those who oppose the current regime."
Savkovic's lawyer, Milorad Ivosevic, called the verdict a "cynical compromise" without legal foundation and vowed to appeal, said human rights workers who monitored the case.
The United States-based Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the verdict in a letter to Bosnian Serb leaders, calling the case "an egregious violation of press freedom".
Ivanko also accused Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation authorities of failing to present evidence to justify holding a Serb man for several weeks on allegations he committed war crimes.
Milorad Marceta was taken off a U.N. relief agency bus last month in northwest Bosnia and federation authorities accused him of committing atrocities in the town of Sanski Most.

But Ivanko said his detention violates terms of an agreement in Rome between Bosnia's factions which requires the arrest of all war crimes suspects to be reviewed and approved by the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
Marceta has not been indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal.
"There is no evidence, whether material or circumstantial, hearsay or otherwise that in any way links Marceta to the charges," Ivanko said. "The defendant should be released."
